name: Nitrogen Assimilation and Ntr Regulation
description: The nitrogen regulation (Ntr) system controls assimilation of nitrogen from poor sources (glutamine, arginine, etc.) when ammonia is limiting. This sophisticated regulatory cascade involves the two-component system NtrB-NtrC, the alternative sigma factor σ54 (RpoN), and the PII signal transduction protein GlnB. The system demonstrates phosphorelay signaling, σ54-dependent transcription activation, and integration of nitrogen status with global metabolism.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on extensive research on nitrogen metabolism regulation, including structural studies of NtrC-σ54 complexes and the PII signal transduction mechanism. The Ntr system is one of the most thoroughly characterized examples of σ54-dependent regulation and two-component signal transduction. All regulatory mechanisms have been validated through genetic, biochemical, and structural studies.

notes: This flowchart represents the Ntr system with 43 unique nodes (A-BF). Contains 2 OR logic gates (nitrogen status check, PII modification state) and 3 AND gates (σ54 activation requires NtrC-P enhancer AND RNAP-σ54; other Ntr genes require NtrC-P AND σ54; feedback requires glutamine AND PII). The system demonstrates σ54-dependent transcription (ATP-dependent open complex formation), PII signal transduction (2-ketoglutarate sensing), and two-component phosphorelay (NtrB-NtrC). All mechanisms validated against structural and biochemical studies.
